transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… the main thing is I keep avoiding work that takes a lot of focused thinking. Reports, planning bigger events across sites—stuff I know matters. I sit down to do it and it feels like I hit a wall, so I put it off.
Do you feel anxious when you think about doing these tasks that require focused thinking?
I don’t know if I’d call it anxious. It’s more like… I just don’t want to start it, and I kind of put it off. I haven’t really thought about it as anxiety.
Do you think you're avoiding these tasks because you're worried you won't do them well?

Not really. I mean, I want them done well, but it’s more that anything that needs me to sit down and really think—like monthly reports or planning across multiple sites—just feels like I hit a wall. So I put it off, even when I know it matters.
Do you have difficulty paying attention to details or making careless mistakes in your work?

Yeah… that does happen. I’ll send out a clinic staffing schedule or even a soccer league email thinking I looked it over, and then someone points out I had the wrong date or left off a location. Stuff I should’ve caught.
Do you often feel tired or lacking in energy?
Not really sure. I mean, I get tired like anyone, but I haven’t noticed it being a big thing.
Do you feel overwhelmed or stressed when you're not able to complete these tasks that require focused thinking?

Yeah, I guess stressed, but mostly because I know it matters and I’m still not getting it done. Like those monthly reports or planning a multi-site event… it feels like I just hit a wall when I have to sit down and really think through it, so I keep pushing it off.
Do you have trouble focusing or avoiding tasks that require a lot of thinking outside of work as well?

Yeah… outside of work too, if it’s something that takes real sitting-down thinking, I tend to put it off. That’s honestly a big part of why I came in. It feels like I hit a wall, even when I know it’s important.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?
I don’t think so. I mean, I can make quick decisions sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’m usually acting without thinking.
Do you often feel sad or depressed?
Not really. I mean, I get frustrated or down on myself sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’m often sad or depressed.
Have you been experiencing this difficulty with focused thinking for a short period or has it been going on for a while?
It’s been going on a while… not just recently. I’d say close to two years now. It seemed to start after my friend died, when I ended up taking on more of the league and outreach stuff.
Do you often feel guilty or worthless about something?
Not really. I mean, I get annoyed with myself when I drop the ball on things, but I wouldn’t say I feel worthless or anything like that.
Do you often find yourself feeling extremely sleepy during the day?
No, not really. I mean, I get tired sometimes like anyone, but I wouldn’t say I’m extremely sleepy during the day.
Has this difficulty with focused thinking and avoiding tasks caused problems in your relationships or daily life outside of work?

Yeah… somewhat. I’m still getting by, mostly, but it’s caused some problems. People have had to cover things I missed, and I’ve had deadlines slip. Outside work too, I’ve had to make those last-minute apology calls or texts to friends, which is… embarrassing.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety when you're sitting still?
Not especially. I might shift around a bit if I’m sitting a long time, but I don’t think of myself as restless or fidgety most of the time.
Have you noticed any problems with your memory, such as forgetting things you normally wouldn't?

Yeah… some. I’ll forget to return calls from volunteers, or miss little errands for events. A couple times a community meeting slipped my mind completely until someone texted me, and then I had to apologize. It’s not constant, but it’s happened enough that I’ve noticed.
Have you noticed any significant decline in your ability to learn new things or understand complex information over the past two years?
No, I don’t think so. I mean, I can still learn things and understand complicated stuff… it just may take me a bit to sit down with it. I haven’t noticed a real decline, though.
Do you feel motivated to do these tasks when you finally get around to doing them?

Sort of… once I’m actually doing it, I know it matters and I want it done. But getting started on anything that takes real sitting-down brain work—like monthly reports or planning a bigger health event—it feels like I hit a wall. I keep putting it off longer than I should.
Do you find yourself being less interested in activities you used to enjoy?
Not really, no. I still like the things I like… I just don’t always get around to them, I guess.
Do you think you would avoid these tasks less if you knew you wouldn't be judged or criticized for your performance?

I don’t think judgment is the main thing, honestly. It’s more that the tasks themselves—like the monthly reports or planning a bigger health event—feel like this wall I have to get over. Even when I know they matter, I keep putting them off.
Do you think your difficulty with starting tasks is related to a fear of not doing them perfectly?

Not really perfection, no. It’s more… anything that needs real sitting-down brain work, like the reports or planning a bigger health event, I just hit a wall with it. I know it matters, but I still put it off.
